learning_outcomes.text: Knows the types and classification of thermal treatments applied to metallic materials.
Understands the principles of phase transformations during heating and cooling processes.
Knows the characteristics of thermochemical (carburizing, nitriding, etc.) and thermomechanical treatments.
Has notions about unconventional thermal treatments and modern methods of material hardening.
Understands the relationship between material structure and mechanical properties resulting from thermal treatment.
Knows the equipment and installations used in thermal and surface treatments.
Identifies and selects appropriate thermal treatments depending on the material and engineering application.
Interprets structural diagrams and transformation curves for analyzing behavior during thermal treatment.
Performs microscopic observations of metallographic structures resulting from different types of treatment.
Applies calculation and design methods for thermal and thermochemical treatment cycles.
Correctly uses specific equipment and performs experimental work in the thermal treatment laboratory.
Writes technical reports and documentation based on the activities performed.
Observes occupational safety regulations specific to working with thermal and chemical installations.
Demonstrates responsibility in using laboratory equipment and interpreting results.
Works autonomously in performing practical work and processing experimental data.
Assumes team roles in laboratory activities and collaborates effectively with colleagues.
Demonstrates interest in deepening knowledge and applying it in real engineering contexts.

syllabus_topics: I. INTRODUCTORY CONCEPTS: Definitions. Classification of thermal treatments. Thermal treatment cycles. Concepts regarding phase transformation conditions. Heating and cooling media.

II. PRELIMINARY THERMAL TREATMENTS: Introductory concepts. Transformation of pearlite into austenite. Austenitic grain. Transformation of austenite upon cooling. Mechanism of austenite transformation into pearlite. Structure of constituents obtained upon cooling of austenite. Homogenization annealing. Normalizing and structure regeneration annealing. Annealing for improving machinability. Recrystallization annealing. Stress relief annealing.

III. FINAL THERMAL TREATMENTS: Hardening. Transformation of austenite into bainite. Transformation of austenite into martensite. Specifics of austenite cooling with variable or constant rates. Conditions imposed during heating for hardening. Conditions imposed during cooling for hardening. Internal stresses (thermal and structural) and their effects. Hardening procedures. Surface hardening. Hardening defects. Tempering. Specifics of thermal treatments applied to carbon and alloy steels.

IV. THERMOCHEMICAL AND THERMOMECHANICAL TREATMENTS: General concepts. Classification of thermochemical treatments. Stages of thermochemical treatments. Carburizing. Nitriding. Carbonitriding. Sulfiding and sulfocyaniding. Chromizing. Aluminizing. Boronizing. Phosphating. Thermal treatments in superheated steam. Thermomechanical treatments.

V. UNCONVENTIONAL THERMAL TREATMENTS: Thermal treatment in magnetic field. Thermal treatments with laser heating. Thermal treatments with ultrashort light sources. Vacuum thermal treatments. Elements of surface engineering. Modern hardening methods by plasma jet deposition.
VI. SPECIFIC THERMAL TREATMENTS FOR CAST IRONS: Malleablizing annealing. Ferritizing annealing. Graphitizing annealing. Spheroidizing annealing. Thermal treatments of grey cast irons.
VII. THERMAL TREATMENT APPLIED TO NON-FERROUS METALS AND ALLOYS: Recrystallization annealing. Stress relief annealing. Homogenization annealing. Hardening and tempering.
VIII. EQUIPMENT NECESSARY FOR THERMAL AND THERMOCHEMICAL TREATMENTS: Heating equipment. Cooling equipment.

IX. THERMAL TREATMENTS APPLIED TO MACHINE PARTS: Thermal treatments applied to forged and die-forged parts. Thermal treatment of shafts and axles. Thermal treatment of bearings. Thermal treatment of springs. Thermal treatment of gears.

X. THERMAL TREATMENTS OF SPECIAL STEELS: Thermal and thermochemical treatments of tool steels. Thermal treatments of wear-resistant steels. Thermal treatments of shock-resistant steels. Thermal treatments of corrosion-resistant steels.
XI. THERMAL TREATMENT OF PARTS: Generalities. Previous thermal treatments. Concomitant thermal treatments. Thermal treatments after welding.

teaching_methods: Discovery-based learning models facilitated by direct and indirect exploration of reality
assessment_rules: The final grade is composed of 60% from the Oral Exam and 40% from Laboratory Activities. A minimum score of 5 is required for both the Oral Exam and Laboratory Activities. All laboratory work must be completed, with recovery allowed for only one pending laboratory session.
